subject: Renewal discussion: amend commit to 16 GPUs and updated monthly commit
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tom Riley <triley@zephyr-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — option to double reserved capacity to 16 GPUs

Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we talked through, your current Dedicated pool (8 GPUs) renews in late June. Based on your projected Q3 throughput and the model mix you shared, we recommend moving to a 16-GPU reserved pool to keep p99 latency within your target while enabling headroom for burst workloads.

Attached is a clean proposal (ZE-4821_proposal_16gpus_v1.pdf) with two term options: a 12-month roll with a 12% unit discount vs your current commit, or a 24-month contract with an 18% discount and guaranteed monthly throughput SLAs. Both options include:
- Dedicated pool: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Monthly commit: prorated token-based billing with fixed baseline, plus burst credits
- Canaries: staged migration plan and performance acceptance tests during week 1 of the renewal

Questions I'm hoping to clarify this week:
1) Do you need firm monthly throughput SLAs or is a best-effort with credits acceptable?
2) Procurement timeline and the signature authority (is Maya the signer?)
3) Any additional compliance artifacts we should surface before legal review

I'll loop legal/Sales Engineering after I have your preferred term. Happy to set a call early next week to review the spreadsheet.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — option to double reserved capacity to 16 GPUs

Hannah —

Appreciate the thorough proposal. A few quick clarifying questions before we loop in procurement/legal:
- Pricing: can you share the per-GPU blended monthly rate behind the two term options? The PDF lists total commit but not the per-unit math.
- SLA: our engineering leadership will insist on p99 latency guarantees for inference peaks; what does Redwood cover for p99 on the 24-month SLA? Specifically, is there a credit structure tied to missed p99 SLOs?
- Migration: we run a heavy caching layer; will the canary plan include KV cache warm-up steps?

Maya — can you confirm if you need a vendor security questionnaire before the commercial terms are signed?

—Tom
Tom Riley
Head of Platform Engineering | Zephyr Analytics

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — option to double reserved capacity to 16 GPUs

Tom — quick tech notes to answer your items: 

Pricing math (high level):
- Baseline monthly commit (12mo option): $X,XXX per GPU equivalent — blended in the proposal to $Y,YYY total. (We can provide the exact line-item spreadsheet on request.)
- 24mo option moves to an 18% blended discount through committed term; per-GPU equivalent falls accordingly.

SLA and credits:
- SLA for 24mo: monthly p99 latency target of <= 220ms for the model family you provided (chat + retrieval-augmented generation).
- Remedies: cumulative credit up to 30% of that month's committed fee after third-party verified incidents or repeated under-performance (we require sample traces and Redwood metrics).

Migration and canary plan (week-by-week):
Week 0: config prep & access
Week 1: staged canary (20% traffic) + KV cache warm-up scripts (we'll coordinate with your infra team)
Week 2: broaden to 50% + full synthetic load tests
Week 3: cutover and rollback window (72 hours)
Acceptance tests: we provide a checklist (latency, token-cost per inference, error-rate) — pass/fail gates before full cutover.

I'll attach the SLA summary in the next email (SLA_amendment_summary.xlsx). Happy to walk through with your infra folks.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@procurement.zephyr.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Tom Riley <triley@zephyr-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — option to double reserved capacity to 16 GPUs

Maya / Tom —

Thanks for the questions. A few commercial/legal clarifications from our side:
- We can include the SLA language in an amendment to your existing Master Services Agreement rather than issuing a brand new contract — should speed up review.
- For a 24-month term we can offer the 18% discount as proposed. If Zephyr needs earlier termination rights for regulatory reasons we can add a limited carve-out with a pro-rated termination fee (negotiable).
- Pricing floor: to maintain capacity reservation we require the full monthly commit regardless of short-term usage; burst credits kick in to cover occasional spikes but do not reduce the committed fee.
- We can add a 30-day technical acceptance period post-cutover; failure during that period triggers remediation steps and defined credits per the SLA doc.

I'll draft a one-page amendment for your review once Hannah confirms the chosen term.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@procurement.zephyr.com>

Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — option to double reserved capacity to 16 GPUs

Hannah / Sean —

We had an internal procurement sync and are comfortable moving forward with the 12-month term at the 12% discount while we validate the new capacity in Q3. Procurement would like the following before signing: 
- A short table that shows the per-GPU blended monthly rate and the total monthly commit (line-item numbers),
- Confirmation that the 72-hour rollback window and the 30-day acceptance period are in the amendment,
- A completed vendor security questionnaire (we have attached ours; if you prefer, point us to the vendor portal).

If you can send the per-GPU math and a one-page amendment draft early next week, we should be able to route for signature by May 31.

Thanks —
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager | Zephyr Analytics
